# Understanding
 
 - COre questions
  - WebR - fully supported see Reprex below
  - Dplyenages current supprots for syntax APIs (some are in preview and not GA)
      - dbplyr
      - dtplyr
      - arrow
      - duckplyr
  - Super excitin that arrow is supported! (+1 for modualrity and iteropertablity!)
  - So dplyeages works on any database dbplyr supports (postgers, duckdb, snowflake ... etc) - IT DOES NOT REQUQIRE OPEN TABLE FORMAT (like duckake)
- How it works
   - each query API produces  a plan (to be evlauted on a lazy object)
   - this pacakge (dplyneage) turns it into a in memory lineage object that is convertable intothe gold-stadnrd lineage JSON shceam (OpenLineage)
   - this lineage object is then visabilze via react flow

# Simple Reprex

Runs in your browser with webR — no R install. Edit the pipeline and hit **Run Code**; the first run downloads packages, so give it a moment.

```{webr}
library(dplyr); library(dbplyr); library(dplyneage)

con <- simulate_postgres()

# layer 1 (silver): clean + derive from raw mtcars
silver <- tbl_lazy(mtcars, con = con, name = "mtcars") |>
  mutate(
    cyl   = as.integer(cyl),
    kpl   = mpg * 0.425,
    heavy = wt > 3.5
  ) |>
  select(cyl, kpl, heavy, hp)

# layer 2 (gold): aggregate, reading from a table named "silver"
silver_cols <- mtcars |>
  mutate(cyl = as.integer(cyl), kpl = mpg * 0.425, heavy = wt > 3.5) |>
  select(cyl, kpl, heavy, hp)

gold <- tbl_lazy(silver_cols, con = con, name = "silver") |>
  summarise(
    avg_kpl  = mean(kpl, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_hp   = mean(hp, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_models = n(),
    .by = c(cyl, heavy)
  )

# names must match: gold's source "silver" stitches to the silver model
lin <- extract_lineage(list(silver = silver, gold = gold))

lin
lineage_flow(lin)
```
